# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan for Two Adults

A calm, station-friendly 4-day Kyoto trip built around temples, neighborhood walks, and local food. I’m assuming a mid-range pace with mostly walking, subway, and buses, and a hotel near Kyoto Station or a major rail hub.

## 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary, Budget, and Rain Backup

| Day | Focus | Main Plan | Rain Backup | Est. Cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr 10 | Higashiyama temples | Kiyomizu-dera early, Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka stroll, Yasaka Shrine, Gion evening walk | Kyoto National Museum + tea break | $210 |
| Apr 11 | Arashiyama and western Kyoto | Tenryu-ji, bamboo grove at opening, Okochi Sanso garden, riverfront walk | Sagano Scenic Railway area cafes + temples with indoor halls | $260 |
| Apr 12 | Quiet north Kyoto | Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, Daitoku-ji area, local lunch in a calmer district | Kyoto Imperial Palace + Nishijin Textile Center | $230 |
| Apr 13 | Central Kyoto and food | Fushimi Inari early, Nishiki Market, Pontocho/Kawaramachi neighborhood time, last shopping | Kyoto Shibori Museum or Kyoto Railway Museum | $220 |

### Day 1: Higashiyama and Gion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in near Kyoto Station, then head to **Kiyomizu-dera** early to avoid crowds.
- Afternoon: Walk the preserved lanes of **Sannenzaka** and **Ninenzaka**, then continue to **Yasaka Shrine** and Maruyama Park.
- Evening: Slow stroll through **Gion** and dinner in a small local restaurant.
- Food: Try yudofu, tofu skin, or a simple kaiseki-style set lunch.

### Day 2: Arashiyama and the West Side
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Tenryu-ji** and the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before tour groups build up.
- Afternoon: Visit **Okochi Sanso Garden** or take a relaxed riverside walk near Togetsukyo Bridge.
- Evening: Return to central Kyoto for an easy dinner near your station.
- Food: Try soba, yuba, or grilled river fish if available.

### Day 3: Quiet Northern Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Start at **Kinkaku-ji**, then continue to **Ryoan-ji** for a calmer temple experience.
- Afternoon: Explore the quieter **Daitoku-ji** temple area and nearby lanes.
- Evening: Keep it low-key with a neighborhood izakaya or noodle shop.
- Food: Look for obanzai, Kyoto-style home cooking, and seasonal vegetables.

### Day 4: Fushimi Inari and Central Kyoto Food Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** at sunrise or very early for the best walking experience.
- Afternoon: Spend time at **Nishiki Market** and nearby shopping streets for snacks and gifts.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: Spend time at **Nishiki Market** and nearby shopping streets for snacks and gifts, Kyoto, Japan
- Evening: Finish with a relaxed walk around **Pontocho** or **Kawaramachi** before departure.
- Food: Sample tamagoyaki, pickles, tofu dishes, and small street snacks from the market.

## Rough Budget for 2 Adults

| Category | Plan | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Hotel | 3 nights near Kyoto Station or Karasuma | $420–$620 |
| Local transit | Subway, bus, JR local rides, occasional taxi | $90–$140 |
| Food | Mix of casual lunches, nice dinners, snacks | $420–$520 |
| Admissions | Temples, gardens, museums, small entry fees | $120–$180 |
| Local extras | Tea, souvenirs, backup indoor activity | $80–$140 |
| Buffer | Weather, taxi, or splurge meal cushion | $150–$220 |
| Total | Kept within your target | **$1,280–$1,820** |

### Budget fit
- To stay safely under **$1,800**, aim for a hotel around **$140–$180/night** before taxes.
- Use transit passes only if they match your route; otherwise pay as you go.
- Keep one nicer dinner and one special tea stop, but otherwise favor lunch sets and local spots.

## Best Stay Area for Easy Transit

- **Kyoto Station area**: best for airport access, JR lines, and luggage convenience.
- **Karasuma / Shijo area**: very good for subway access, food, and walking.
- **Avoid** staying too far east if you want the easiest station access and less transit time.
